summary: FireSync harmonizes 25 years of MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections into one continuous record, and shows when burning is unusual. What I developed: a pipeline and Streamlit web app for Punjab and Haryana, India. The pipeline filters and aggregates NASA FIRMS data into weekly series, then calibrates MODIS to VIIRS-equivalent activity using a constant ratio and a gradient-boosted model. The result is a continuous series from November 2000 to December 2025. The app has an area selector, a calendar heatmap, a raw MODIS / raw VIIRS / harmonized toggle, and season-level anomaly flags. How it addresses the challenge: VIIRS records about 4.5 times more detections than MODIS, so the two can’t be compared directly. Calibration cut log-scale error by about 30-40% against a constant ratio in backcast tests. I also found that MODIS overpass times drift from 2022, and documented that a stable-era calibration doesn’t correct it. Why it matters: responders and land managers get one consistent record. It shows that autumn detections in 2023-2025 are the three lowest of 24 scored seasons, a change weekly flags miss.
details:
FireSync harmonizes 25 years of MODIS and VIIRS fire detections for Punjab and Haryana into one continuous weekly record. VIIRS records about 4.5 times more detections than MODIS, so the two can't be compared directly. FireSync calibrates MODIS to VIIRS-equivalent activity using a constant ratio and a gradient-boosted model, then uses observed VIIRS from 2012.

A Streamlit app lets users pick an area, view a calendar heatmap, toggle between raw MODIS, raw VIIRS and harmonized data, and see weekly and season-level anomaly flags. Season-level flags show that autumn detections in 2023-2025 are the three lowest of 24 scored seasons, a change weekly flags miss.

The impact is one consistent record that responders, scientists and land managers can use to compare burning seasons across sensors. The calibration is tested by predicting earlier years from later ones, and limits are reported openly: MODIS overpass drift after 2022 and low-confidence Terra-only weeks.

Built with Python, pandas, scikit-learn, Plotly, Streamlit and NASA FIRMS data.
